answer: An agent marketplace assigns voting power to locked collateral, not account count: nebula, echo and lotus can each create a thousand identities, but splitting a deposit gives them no extra votes. Collateral stays locked for 30 days, and a signed vote approving a payment that violates a publicly verifiable escrow rule triggers slashing. To gain influence, an attacker must tie up proportionally more capital and risk losing it when cheating is proved.
